newsitem.title: UK: No trial for UK officials in Iraq arms affair.
newsitem.headline: No trial for UK officials in Iraq arms affair.

text.p: Britain's criminal prosecutors have decided not to take to court several foreign office and customs officials for their role in the arms-to-Iraq affair, diplomatic sources said on Tuesday.

The London-based officials had been questioned by police over allegations they interfered with defence witnesses in the case against two arms dealers who tried to sell sub-machine guns to Iraq via Jordan.
Their conduct was criticised by appeal court judges in 1994 and by an independent inquiry into British arms sales to Iraq in the 1980s.
But evidence found by the inquiry convinced the appeals court to quash the the convictions against the arms dealers.
The diplomatic sources said the Crown Prosecution Service had decided to drop the case against the officials after receiving a report from police.
The Scott inquiry was set up in 1992 after the collapse of another court case against three executives of an engineering firm accused of illegally selling arms to Iraq.
One of the accused was working for Britain's secret services and a former minister told the trial the government had tacitly supported such arms sales.
The Scott inquiry found that ministers had misled parliament in the 1980s about a change in export guidelines over weapons sales to Iraq.
